info.bio:
En la época de la new wave existió en el Reino Unido un grupo de artistas que crearon, sin perder en sus textos lugar para el comentario social y político, movidos ritmos inspirados por el ska jamaicano, al que impregnaban de pop y punk.
Así, al estilo de los Specials, The Selecter o Madness, se formó en 1979 en la ciudad de Birmingham The Beat, un conjunto compuesto por el cantante y guitarrista Dave Wakeling, el cantante Ranking Roger, el guitarrista Andy Cox

scenes.name: 2-Tone: The Specials y el ska de los Midlands
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El sello de Jerry Dammers llenó en 1979 el hueco de un punk bailable: The Specials, siete músicos blancos y negros de Coventry (Terry Hall y su mirada heredada de Rotten, el rude boy Neville Staple), cruzan el ska de Prince Buster con la energía punk y un realismo social en blanco y negro («Gangsters», «Too Much Too Young», «Concrete Jungle», «Nite Klub»). El damero blanco y negro simboliza la integración racial; The Beat (Handsworth: «Mirror in the Bathroom», «Stand Down Margaret»), The Selecter («On My Radio») y Madness suman cinco hits en cinco singles. El sueño de un «nuevo Motown» se convierte en «un monstruo»: More Specials se refugia en la música ligera y la caja de ritmos, y «Ghost Town» (1981), retrato de la desindustrialización, llega al número uno mientras arden las ciudades. Fun Boy Three, «Nelson Mandela» y el fin. Posmoderno antes del new pop: «Estamos trayendo de vuelta algo que nunca existió».

xref.title: The English Beat – Mirror in the Bathroom (1980); Held Out Against Violence and Racism Through Music; Second Wave Ended ~1985
xref.body: The English Beat, led by Dave Wakeling, were formed in the late 1970s and had their first hit with "Mirror in the Bathroom" (1980), a classic of the great ska revival. The second wave of ska — spanning roughly 1979 to 1985 — was vibrant and carried a hopeful message as a positive alternative to hard economic times and racial riots in Britain. By the mid-1980s, Jerry Dammers was broke and Two-Tone was falling apart under huge debt; despite efforts by the Clash, the Beat, and Bad Manners, the second wave ended around 1985. "Ska was a positive alternative to the hard economic times and the racial riots that were plaguing Britain in the early 1980s."

xref.title: 1950s Greenwich Village Singer
xref.body: Connie Converse was a singer on the Ascense in the 1950s, gaining recognition within the Beat Nick crowd in Greenwich Village. Despite her talent, her career didn't flourish as she had hoped. "The Converse was a singer on the Ascense in the 1950s, making her name with the Beat Nick Crowd and Greenwich Village."

xref.title: Influence on Ska Punk
xref.body: The English Beat, along with The Specials, played a vital role in shaping the post-punk world and are considered instrumental in the development of Ska punk. "It weren't for bands like the beat and the specials. Would we have all the Scott punk that we have today?"

xref.title: Intellectual and Literary Figure
xref.body: Richie was the intellectual force behind the Manic Street Preachers, well-versed in figures like Karl Marx, Albert Camus, Sylvia Plath, Dostoevsky, JD Salinger, Jack Kerouac, and Joseph Conrad, as well as the Beat Poets. He meticulously rehearsed philosophical and literary quotes for interviews, solidifying his role as the band's literary expert. "Richie knew about Karl Marx, Albert Kamu, Sylvia Plath, Dostoevsky, JD Salinger, Jack Kerawak, Joseph Conrad, and all the beat poets."

xref.title: Popularizer of the "Bo Diddley Beat"
xref.body: Bo Diddley is renowned for using a particular rhythm so effectively that it became known as the "Bo Diddley beat." Although the beat itself originated at least 50 years before his time, he was instrumental in introducing it to rock and roll, influencing numerous artists from Iggy Pop to Joan Jett. "Bow didn't invent that beat. It's history goes back at least 50 years, but he was the one who introduced it to rock and roll."

xref.title: Producer of "Old Town Road" Beat
xref.body: Young Kio, a Dutch record producer, created the beat for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" by manipulating a sample from Nine Inch Nails' instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" and selling it for $30 on his online store, where Lil Nas X purchased it. His real name is Kioa Rokima. "He stumbled upon a track called 34 Ghosts 4, an instrumental from the 2008 Nine-H Nails album Ghost 1-4."

xref.title: Producer of "Old Town Road" Beat
xref.body: Young Kioh, a Dutch producer, created the beat for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" based on Nine Inch Nails' "34 Ghosts 4." Lil Nas X purchased this beat online for $30. Young Kioh was unaware of the beat's use until the song became a massive hit. Through a quiet negotiation, he received songwriting credits, a share of the profits, and shared in the Grammy wins for the song. "He found a Dutch kid by the name of Young Kioh, who had created a beat based on a track called 34 Ghosts 4."

xref.title: Success in Europe (Germany and UK)
xref.body: Despite US struggles, Billy Talent achieved significant success in Europe, particularly Germany and the UK. This was attributed to extensive touring in small clubs on their first album, opening for bands like The Beatsteaks, and strong label support that ensured radio and MTV play. They prioritized investing their time and energy in Europe, playing festivals there due to a strong "festival culture," rather than "half sold rooms" in the States. "we put in the time there. We played every small club in Germany on the first album and we got the right tours opening up for the one of the best punk bands there called the Beat Stakes. And it just took off organically."
